scope: Release-level redistribution review, not a file/header-complete SPDX SBOM or legal clearance

submodulesChanged.contrib/jemalloc: bumped; not linked (only DB::ServerSetting names match 'jemalloc')
submodulesChanged.contrib/gdeflate: added; linked on all four platforms

changesFromPrevious.licenseFileCorrections: License records now name the files actually reproduced in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt (e.g. xz COPYING/COPYING.0BSD, rocksdb LICENSE.Apache/LICENSE.leveldb, lz4 lib/LICENSE, each AWS C library, LLVM runtime LICENSE files).

evidenceLimits: Both macOS archives retain library-prefixed members and are fully covered by the target-family mapping; an unmapped group fails record generation.

Linux archives are chdb-core's split archive: nine relocatable shards each, cut across library boundaries. Critical LGPL and platform-specific libraries are verified by defined symbol anchors; remaining libraries are not individually reconstructed from the shards.

symbolCount counts distinct defined symbol names (nm --defined-only, local symbols included), so it is not comparable with the v26.11.1 counts. The split archive makes most symbols local, so anchors are matched with or without the .chdb suffix.
Header-only/transitive code is not completely enumerated by archive member names. License and notices collection must preserve bundled component texts.
A registry type label is heuristic, not the authoritative file license. XZ/liblzma, LLVM, ICU, libarchive, vectorscan, librdkafka and RocksDB illustrate the distinction.
